title: Seeing Things
text:
Most patterns are mostly noise. Here’s how to tell.
We’re brilliant at spotting patterns, and just as good at seeing things that aren’t there. Every exhibit in this museum pairs a real dataset with one clear picture, the statistical technique that tests it, and the brain trap that makes us misread it.

title: Seeing Things
text:
The wings

The Cabinet of Coincidences: correlations that look meaningful and aren’t.
Mostly Noise: chance, luck and streaks.
Decision Corridor: what actually causes what.
The Lab: testing ideas properly.

title: About
text:
Seeing Things is a museum of patterns: a collection of short data stories that each ask a simple question, test it honestly, and give a verdict (causal, confounded, coincidence, reverse causation, or inconclusive).
Under every chart, the Looking Glass shows the exact SQL, Python and R that built it, so nothing has to be taken on trust.
It’s built by Abby Brazell, a data analyst in the Bay of Plenty, Aotearoa New Zealand, as a personal project using openly licensed public data. The code is on GitHub.
